description: A message written while the agent is busy with a turn: not sent yet, it waits in the queue just under the conversation (above the composer), drawn as your bubble but grey. Hovering its row shows delete, send-now and edit buttons beside it. On the phone, a message is also queued when it's sent while the chat's host isn't reached, with a small dim cloud left of its bubble till the host is back. A message sent while the host wasn't reached stays in the queue, on disk, till the host says it took it; one the host says no to stays there with a warning in place of the cloud, saying why, and goes again only by its send-now button.
opens: Enter in the composer (with text or attachments) while a turn runs
Sending while the chat's host isn't reached (the phone)

parts.name: bubble
parts.shows: Same shape and content as a sent message's bubble (attachments row, then markdown text), right-aligned, but filled with the text colour at 7% and its text at 55% opacity (grey), not the accent. Queued messages stack 10px apart, oldest first, below the last message of the chat and above the composer; the queue takes no room when empty.

parts.name: buttons
parts.shows: Three small round flat buttons (24px) in a row just left of the bubble, their middle level with the middle of its last line of text, invisible until the pointer is on the row, fading in over 150ms: ✕ (close icon), ↑ (a bold arrow character), and the circular-arrows revert icon. They stay beside the bubble whatever the message ends with (a list, a numbered list, a code block).

decisions.said: A bullet or numbered list on a message's last line pushes the Send now / Revert buttons well out of place
decisions.rule: Every app keeps a message's buttons just beside its bubble, level with its last line, whatever the message ends with (a list, a numbered list, a code block): what's inside a bubble never widens the bubble's share of the row

decisions.said: On mobile a single click of a user message should reveal the revert, send now .etc buttons
decisions.rule: Every app shows a message's buttons without hover where there is none: on a touch screen a single tap on the message shows them (a long press too) and another tap hides them; with a pointer, hovering its row shows them

decisions.said: Said buttons must be center aligned with the text on the last line of the message it is not so at the moment
decisions.rule: Every app centres a message's buttons on the middle of the bubble's last line of text, at any text size

phone.does: A tap on the message shows the same buttons, centred on its last line of text as here; another tap hides them. A long press shows them too
phone.why: No hover on touch; the owner asked for a single tap

actions.does: Drops it from the queue. Tooltip "Delete this queued message".

Sends this message and every queued message before it at once, together as one message (their texts joined by a blank line, their attachments together), to the turn going on, which isn't stopped: claude, Codex and pi take it in between the turn's steps and go on; Apple's on-device model, which answers in one call, takes it once its turn is over. In a Claude Code chat, every command and subagent running in the foreground is moved to the background as it's sent (Claude Code's background_tasks, as its Ctrl+B), where it goes on: the turn's step that waits on it ends, so the turn takes the message in now instead of once they're done, and stops none of them; their cards read running in background. Codex and pi have no way to move a running call: a message sent while one runs is taken in once it ends, and nothing is stopped. The sent message is drawn as sent where the chat has got to. With a revert waiting to be made, the revert is made first, as sending does, stopping the turn, and the messages go after it. Tooltip "Send now: send this and the queued messages before it, without stopping the chat".

decisions.said: Agents still seem to stop on send queeud message, this is not ideal
decisions.rule: Every app's send-now on a queued message gives it to the agent's turn going on without stopping it, for every agent that can take a message mid-turn; one that can't takes it as its turn ends

decisions.said: Getting a queued message into a Claude chat without it killing all the chat's running subagents is very hard, close to impossible, and a massive problem
decisions.rule: Every app's send-now on a queued message moves the agent's foreground commands and subagents to the background first, where its agent can (Claude Code), so the message reaches the agent at once and every subagent keeps running; an agent that can't move them takes the message in once the running call ends, stopping nothing

actions.does: Takes it out of the queue and puts its text in the composer before what's already written there (separated by a blank line), caret after its text, its attachments back in the composer's strip. Tooltip "Edit: put this message back in the box".

states.name: turn ends by itself
states.shows: Every queued message is sent at once, together as one message (texts joined by blank lines); they leave the queue and the sent message appears in the chat as a normal sent bubble.

states.name: turn stopped (Esc / stop button)

decisions.said: You can get into a state where messages are queued, but the agent is not currently owrking / it is interrupted. Once interrupted, queued messsges should automatically be sent into te model.
decisions.rule: Every app sends the queue when a turn ends, whether it ended by itself or was interrupted

states.shows: Once the stopped turn ends, the queue is sent as when a turn ends by itself: all of it as one message.

states.name: another chat opened
states.shows: The queue stays with the chat it was written in, kept beside that chat's draft (on disk on the phone, over a restart on the desktop), and is drawn under its conversation again, as it was, when the chat is opened again. A new chat's queue goes into its box instead.

decisions.said: Going to another chat and back un-queues a queued message; queued messages should persist across chats (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app keeps a chat's queued messages with that chat when another is opened, draws them again when it's opened, and sends them to it when its turn ends meanwhile

states.name: turn ends while another chat is open
states.shows: The left chat's queue is sent to it as its turn ends, by itself or stopped, as if it were open: all of it as one message. The sent message is in that chat's conversation when it is opened. Only a turn's end the app sees sends it; one sent whose host may not have taken it goes back to the front of the queue and is sent again by the same uuid, which its host takes once.

states.name: in history
states.shows: A message Claude Code recorded as sent mid-turn (queued_command) is drawn in a reopened chat as an ordinary sent message (UserTurn).

decisions.said: Nearly all of the phone's disconnects come from the screen turning off or the app being put away: design for Android closing connections, cache more, and instead of a red box show a cloud, with leeway and messages queued while the connection is down (paraphrased)
decisions.rule: Every app that queues while its host isn't reached gives each queued message its own uuid as it's written, sends each by that uuid once the host is back and the chat's transcript has been read up to date (so one the host already took is seen and not sent), and puts a message whose link went before the host answered back in the queue by the same uuid, never in the box with a not-sent line: a host takes a message once, whatever the link did.
